title: Coefficient 4 at exponent 1 for the fixed subspace-polynomial affine disperser family: C_B2(f_n) >= 4n - o(n)

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The one fixed total family of proof.md Section 1 and family.md Section 2, the Ben-Sasson-Kopparty subspace-polynomial affine disperser at p=2: f_0(empty)=0; for n>=1 let k be the least prime strictly larger than 2*n^(3/5), r=ceil(n/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)); let A be one fixed deterministic polynomial-time algorithm which on input k outputs a monic irreducible q_k in F_2[Z] of degree k, and put K=F_2[Z]/(A(k)) (the family is defined by A, and the evaluator runs the same A, so definition and evaluation agree; deterministic polynomial-time constructions of such q_k are classical, e.g. Adleman-Lenstra 1986 and Shoup 1989 Section 3); let iota:F_2^n->K^r pad x with r*k-n zeros, cut it into r blocks of k bits, and read each block in the basis 1,Z,...,Z^(k-1); let pi:K->F_2 be the coefficient of Z^0; put y_i=iota_i(x)^(2^(i+1)-1) and f_n(x)=pi(sum over t-element subsets I of [r] of prod_{i in I} y_i). One fixed deterministic algorithm evaluates f_n at every length (family.md Lemma 3.1), so the yes-language is in P and hence in NP with the empty witness and witness bound 0 (family.md Corollary 3.2). f_n is an affine disperser for dimension d(n)=floor(6*n^(4/5))+1, proved in disperser.md Parts I-VIII (family.md Corollary 4.2).","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform NP family, in the full Li-Yang B2 model at actual input length n=|x| (deterministic acyclic circuits, one output, fan-in two, all 16 binary operations, unbounded depth and fan-out, gates counted once with inputs, wires and output selection free, exact computation on every input, nonuniform circuits allowed): C_B2(f_n) >= 4n - 10*d(n) = 4n - 60*n^(4/5) - O(1) for every integer n >= 16807, by gate-elimination.md Theorem 10.1 applied to family.md Corollary 4.2. Consequently liminf_n C_B2(f_n)/n >= 4: for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n) >= (4-epsilon)*n for every integer n >= N_epsilon. The full guarantee is the polynomial_log expression g(n)=4*n^1*(log2 n)^0*(log2 log2 n)^0, and the declared projection is the finite pair (coefficient 4, exponent 1). No sublinear-dimension affine disperser is assumed to require more than 4n gates; nothing about p>1 is claimed.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Unscored refinement of the same theorem: for the same fixed family of proof.md Section 1, every integer n >= 16807 satisfies C_B2(f_n) >= 4n - 10*d(n) with d(n) = floor(6*n^(4/5)) + 1, that is C_B2(f_n) >= 4n - 60*n^(4/5) - 10 (proof.md Sections 4-5, from gate-elimination.md Theorem 10.1 applied to family.md Corollary 4.2). This is the quantitative remainder behind the declared projection; it does not assert any coefficient above 4 and does not assert any exponent above 1.

Unscored model lemma (gate-elimination.md Theorem 10.1): for every n >= 1, every function g: F_2^n -> F_2 that is an affine disperser for dimension d in the sense of family.md Definition 1.1 with 0 <= d < n satisfies C_B2(g) >= 4n - 10d in the full B2 model, by the five-case gate-elimination analysis of gate-elimination.md Sections 2-8 with the potential W = s + 4q + 6I and the per-iteration bound dW <= 10 da.

Unscored disperser lemma (disperser.md Part VII, Theorem VII.1): for integers t < r and a prime k with k >= r(r+1)/t, and for every mu != 0, the function f(x_1,...,x_r) = Tr(mu * sum over t-subsets I of prod_{i in I} x_i^(2^(i+1)-1)) on K^r is nonconstant on every affine subspace of dimension greater than kr/t + kt + r(r+1), where K = F_(2^k); with the family parameters of family.md Section 2 this threshold is at most 6n^(4/5), giving family.md Theorem 4.1.
